reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Kastner and the Wild Side crew predicted over 30 pounds of black bass winning the two-day tournament, forecasting 15-pound bags for two days at least for the top teams, but the winning team managed 27 pounds. The “big bass” topped out at just 4.6 pounds, where expectations were at least three being 8 or more pounds. Part if this, Kastner explained, was that many anglers were using bigger baits than the bass were seeking, and for anglers on Hamilton this week, he urges them to downsize their baits. Bass are chasing smaller shad now, so downsize those shad-looking baits.

reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Lots of big black bass are being seen on the shoreline chasing bream, and they are scattered from shallow to 60 feet, biting on a variety of baits top to bottom, points and secondary points best. Crappie are 15 feet down to 50 feet scattered as well; stay with bait and use jigs, minnows or crankbaits.
Bass fishing is getting better, and they are catching schooling fish on the lower end of the lake on CC Spoons and topwaters like Zara Spooks and Rebel Pop-Rs. Also there is an improving bass bite on Carolina rigs in 10-15 feet of water around points. Crappie that are relating to the standing timber are biting well on Crappie Magnets in natural shad, pink or purple colors in 15 feet of water,

reports.text: Crappie are good as they move closer to the shoreline with October around the corner. Black bass remain active around the shoreline with anglers appearing to catch good numbers and in decent sizes, but they’re not suggesting any specific baits (like we said last week, this time of year seems good there for a topwater like a Zara Spook or Rebel Pop-R around the bank).

Black bass are continue biting well. Try a topwater bait such as Zara Spook, as well as worms and buzzbaits. Catfishing picked back up some with good results this week. Noodles baited with nightcrawlers were hooking hungry cats. reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing is trying its best to transition to the fall patterns, but the ongoing warm temps are not letting that happen effectively, so we would call fishing “fair.”
Bass have slowed down during daylight hours and have become hesitant to bite much at all.
Night fishing for bass is good to excellent right now, however! During the nighttime hours bass really pick up and can be readily caught in very shallow areas near main lake creeks and channels. Buzzbaits in dark colors with a large profile trailer bait like a Craw- or Beaver-style bait. Run this or a Chatterbait down dock edges and let the fun begin. Good fish and good numbers can be caught right now!

reports.text: Crappie are eating minnows and jigs floating around at 30 feet deep for the most part. Black bass are super shallow, mid-depth, out in 60 feet and also feeding on the surface at certain times.

reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: “Bass were biting early morning until around 9:30 a.m. Crappie are good with anglers using jigs and worms. Use spinnerbaits or topwater baits for the good bass bite.

reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Dardanelle State Park hosted the second annual DAV Big Bass Tournament on Aug. Many 4- and 5-pound bass were weighed during the two-day event. The overall Big Bass, caught on the first day, weighed 5.69 pounds.
Largemouth bass have been good. Crappie has been fair with minnows and jigs around deep trees with no current.

reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in limbo right now with many largemouth making an attempt to move into shallower areas of the lake. Lots of little fish like spotted bass cannot resist these setups. No crappie report.

reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Westrock Landing (501-658-5598) on Highway 10 near Roland says largemouth bass are fair. Some reports coming in this week say the black bass can be found in 8-12 feet and 16-20 feet. Better bass numbers were evident last week as the Friday night Bass League weigh in had Robert Kinslow and Sam Drennon winning with a 14.74-pound stringer and a Big Bass of 4.48 pounds. Kentucky bass are fair. Some can still be found mixed in with the crappie on the flats or near brush piles in 8-12 feet. Crappie are slow.

reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. Black bass are biting topwater plugs and plastic worms, with good results.

reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) said black bass are fair to good. No reports on crappie.

reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been poor. Black bass are fair, with best success coming on plastic worms.

reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouths continue in their typical, full-blown summer patterns. The bass have become lethargic over the past week and the bite subdued. Once the sun climbs and begins surface penetration, the surface temp will climb several degrees and the bass retreat to the first and second drops out of the flats and deeper sections of the creeks or the river behind primary and secondary points out of river current. “It appears to us the largemouth bass continue feeding at night,” Mike said. “Some mornings when we arrive at dawn, we can hear bass breaking shallow before we ever get to them and it’s apparent we are arriving at the tail end of their cooler-surface-temp, overnight feeding binges. reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing (870-241-3731) said that anglers are having good success catching black bass and bream now.

reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouth have been hitting well on single hook streamers. Waterfalls are key areas for smallmouth. The bass hide under the boulders to get away from the heat.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Black bass also are good. No reports for crappie, catfish or walleye.

reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Bass are doing good around brushtops and structure around the banks with spinners and crankbaits. Crappie are slow but still catching some good ones in 7-9 feet of water around stumps.
